lines.text: {a} cooks something that's almost soup. {b} takes seconds.
Don't tell anyone, but that was good.
{a} and {b} play cards on an upturned crate. Nobody wins. Nobody cares.
Again. Best of nine.
{a} can't sleep. {b} sits up with them by the radio until the static sounds like rain.
Late at night, {a} hums something old. After a while, {b} knows the words.
My mother used to sing that.
{a} says it's {b}'s birthday. It might not be. Nobody checks.
Happy birthday. I made you a candle out of a candle.
{a} fixes the leaking pipe over {b}'s bunk without being asked.
{a} tells the worst joke the bunker has ever heard. {b} laughs anyway, then can't stop.
{a} and {b} sit in silence for an hour. It's the good kind.
{a} and {b} talk about what they'll do when it's over. They make a promise.
Deal. You and me.
{a} says {b} took more than their share. Voices rise. Someone kicks a crate.
Count it yourself, then.
{b} snores. {a} throws a boot. Things escalate.
{a} leaves half a ration on {b}'s bunk. No note. {b} eats it.
...Thanks. I guess.
{a} and {b} argue about the map for an hour. Both are a little right.
{a} teaches {b} how to splint a finger. They practice on each other, badly.
{b} wakes up shouting. {a} is already there with water.
It's alright. You're in the bunker. You're home.
{a} and {b} take turns at the periscope, naming the shapes in the dark.
